results.title: Lions beat Tigers to even up KBO postseason series
results.content: DAEGU — The Samsung Lions launched two home runs to beat up on the Kia Tigers 8-3 to even up their South Korean baseball postseason series Tuesday. Cleanup Lewin Diaz smoked a two-run home run, and the 42-year-old veteran Choi Hyoung-woo blasted a solo shot as the Lions took the second game of this best-of-five series in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) at Daegu Samsung Lions Park in the southeastern city of Daegu. Starter Ariel Jurado pitched 6 2/3 strong innings for his first career postseason victory. At 42 years, 10 months and 11 days old, Choi became the oldest player to play and get a hit, a home run and an RBI in a KBO postseason game. The Lions pounded out nine hits before a sellout crowd of 23,550, after managing only two hits in a 5-1 loss in Monday's series opener. results.title: Convenience stores jump on Korea's rice cake dessert boom
results.content: From butter to toppings, Korean rice cakes — called "tteok" — are enjoying a heyday of flavor innovation. As various rice cake desserts lead this year’s food trends, even spawning the term “tteok-run” to refer to lining up before a store opens to secure the trendy treats, convenience store chains are jumping on the bandwagon. According to purchasing data from market research firm Embrain, estimated spending on rice cakes reached 151.9 billion won ($112 million) from September last year to August this year, up 31.2 percent from the previous year. Spending increased by more than 20 percent across all age groups, with purchases by people in their 20s and younger surging 45.5 percent. The rise reflects a growing number of young consumers willing to wait in long lines to try rice cake desserts that have gone viral on social media. results.title: Cold wave advisories take effect across Korea
results.content: Much of Korea will wake up to freezing temperatures Wednesday, as chilly air sweeping in from the northwest brings morning lows below zero in inland areas. Cold wave advisories are in effect across most of the country. Morning temperatures are forecast to range from minus 2 to 7 degrees Celsius nationwide. Parts of northeastern Gyeonggi Province, Gangwon Province, North Chungcheong Province and inland areas of the south are expected to see temperatures dip below freezing, with frost and icy conditions possible in places. Daytime highs will range from 11 to 17 degrees. Forecast lows and highs in major cities are 2 and 13 degrees Celsius in Seoul; 3 and 12 in Incheon; 1 and 13 in Daejeon; 3 and 15 in Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City; 1 and 14 in Daegu; 5 and 15 in Ulsan; and 7 and 17 in Busan. Strong winds will make it feel even colder, particularly in southern parts of the countr

results.title: 3 ex-officials appeal to top court over 2019 deportation of N. Koreans
results.content: Three former government officials on Tuesday appealed an appellate ruling sentencing them to suspended prison terms for forcibly repatriating two North Korean fishermen in 2019, taking the case to the Supreme Court, sources said. Last week, the Seoul High Court upheld a lower court's guilty verdicts for Chung Eui-yong, former national security adviser; former National Intelligence Service Director Suh Hoon; and former Unification Minister Kim Yeon-chul. All three served in former President Moon Jae-in's administration in November 2019, when Seoul deported two North Korean fishermen back to North Korea after they were captured near the eastern maritime border. The fishermen had been accused of killing 16 fellow crew members on their vessel. A lower court found all three former officials guilty but deferred their sentencing. results.title: Citibank Korea appoints new CEO in 1st leadership change in 6 years
results.content: Citibank Korea has appointed Kim Kyoung-ho, its head of corporate banking, as its new CEO, ending a six-year leadership run under his predecessor, the lender said Tuesday. Kim succeeds Yoo Myung-soon, who became the bank’s first female CEO in 2020. He will serve a three-year term. Kim joined Citibank Korea in 2001 and has held a series of senior positions in corporate banking, including large corporate banking and financial institutions coverage, before being promoted to executive vice president in 2021. On Sept. 22, the lender’s executive recommendation committee named him its sole candidate for the top post. His appointment comes as Citi continues to reshape its Korean operations following its exit from consumer banking. With corporate banking now at the core of its local business, Kim’s challenge as an incoming chief will be to build on that strategic shift and ensure its strong perfo

results.title: Tigers manager not surprised by opponent's lineup changes in KBO postseason
results.content: Kia Tigers manager Lee Bum-ho said Tuesday he was not surprised by substantial changes to the lineup of his Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) postseason opponent. The Tigers beat the Samsung Lions 5-1 to begin their best-of-five series at Daegu Samsung Lions Park in the southeastern city of Daegu on Monday. The Lions, after managing just two hits in the loss, put veteran slugger Choi Hyoung-woo back in the lineup for Tuesday. Outfielder Park Seung-kyu moved up from the No. 5 spot to the No. 2 hole in the order, too. Choi was held out of the lineup initially because there was no designated spot available for him, and he is largely regarded as a defensive liability. But Park said earlier in the day he will prioritize offense in Game 2. results.title: Instant photo kiosk featuring President Lee set to open at presidential house annex
results.content: An instant four-cut photo kiosk will open at an annex of the presidential house in Seoul, allowing visitors to take photos with images of President Lee Jae Myung, his office said Tuesday. The photo booth will go into service at Sarangchae, a public pavilion annexed to Cheong Wa Dae on Wednesday, marking the first anniversary of Lee's presidency, the presidential office said. Visitors can choose from 32 photo frames featuring Lee; his wife, first lady Kim Hea Kyung; or images of Korean cultural heritage assets before taking photos with them and downloading the photos on their smartphones, according to the office.

results.title: Korea hosts G20 global financial stability conference in Seoul
results.content: Korea's finance ministry on Tuesday hosted a global conference bringing together experts to discuss financial stability and supply chains in the era of artificial intelligence (AI). The Ministry of Finance and Economy and the state-run Korea Development Institute co-hosted the G20 Global Financial Stability Conference 2026 in Seoul, an annual event first held in 2013 to discuss ways to address global financial challenges. Around 300 financial experts from across the globe participated in this year's event, discussing ways to enhance the stability and resilience of the global economy and address risks and challenges arising from AI-driven innovation, according to the ministry. In his opening remarks, Second Vice Finance Minister Huh Chang stressed the spread of AI and the restructuring of supply chains could pose new threats to financial market stability. results.title: Foreign tourist arrivals in Korea estimated to have set annual record early
results.content: Foreign tourist arrivals in Korea this year are estimated to have already set an all-time annual record, the culture ministry said Tuesday. Preliminary figures from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism showed that this year's arrivals reached about 18.91 million through Monday, and the total is believed to have surpassed the previous annual record of 18.94 million, set last year, Tuesday, with more than two months left in the year. The ministry expects about 1.94 million people to visit next month if the current trend continues, with the annual total topping 20 million for the first time in the third week of November. Culture, Sports and Tourism Minister Chae Hwi-young said breaking the annual record more than two months early has brought the government's ambitious year-end target of 23 million foreign visitors "within reach." results.title: Kolmar vice chairman confident in K-beauty's continued growth
results.content: Kolmar Group Vice Chairman Yoon Sang-hyun expressed confidence in K-beauty’s continued growth at Amazon Beauty in Seoul 2026 on Tuesday. Yoon delivered a presentation on the sustainability of K-beauty, highlighting the industry's growth potential, driven by the emergence of new brands and an ecosystem connecting product developers with global consumers. Kolmar Korea has served as the event’s exclusive manufacturing sponsor for three consecutive years since its launch in 2024. Amazon Beauty in Seoul is an annual conference and networking event that helps Korean beauty brands expand into overseas markets through Amazon’s global e-commerce platform. “The driving force behind K-beauty’s growth is the constant emergence of new brands,” Yoon said. “With a good idea, ODM (original development manufacturing) companies like Kolmar Korea can develop products, while global platforms like Amazon con

results.title: Veteran hitter returns as Lions manager makes lineup changes after KBO postseason loss
results.content: DAEGU — Samsung Lions manager Park Jin-man made notable changes to his lineup for the second game of the ongoing postseason series against the Kia Tigers on Tuesday, willing to sacrifice defense in hopes of waking up his dormant offense. Veteran designated hitter Choi Hyoung-woo returned to the lineup after being benched for the 5-1 loss in Game 1 of the second round in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) postseason Monday. With the usual left fielder Koo Ja-wook just back from a hamstring injury and unable to take the field, Park kept Koo's bat in the lineup as designated hitter for Game 1 while inserting more defensively sound Park Seung-kyu in left field. Choi, one of the oldest players in the KBO at 42, is considered a defensive liability in the outfield. results.title: No casualties reported in shanty town fire in southern Seoul
results.content: A fire broke out at a shantytown in Seoul's posh southern district of Gangnam on Tuesday, but no casualties have been reported so far, officials said. The fire broke out at about 3:50 p.m. at a makeshift building at Guryong Village, prompting 39 residents to flee to safety, according to fire authorities. Fire authorities issued a Level 1 emergency response at 3:59 p.m. and later raised the response level by one notch as the fire spread. A total of 232 personnel and 70 pieces of equipment were mobilized to the scene to fight the blaze. No injuries or missing persons have been reported so far, and 39 residents have evacuated the area on their own, officials said. Authorities have guided the locals to a safe area and deployed six firefighting helicopters to prevent the blaze from spreading into a wildfire. Firefighting officials plan to look into the cause of the blaze and assess the damage

results.title: S. Korea withdraws 8 diplomatic personnel from Ukraine: FM Cho
results.content: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that South Korea has withdrawn eight diplomatic personnel from Ukraine amid a dispute over Kyiv's disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs). Cho made the remarks during a parliamentary audit of the foreign ministry, saying that despite the partial withdrawal, he has continued communication with the Ukraine foreign minister to resolve the issue. South Korea recalled its ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang, earlier this month and decided to withdraw some embassy personnel, citing Kyiv's failure to take steps to resolve the dispute and persistent threats of Russian airstrikes. "Eight have been withdrawn so far," Cho said, adding that the withdrawal had been unavoidable given Ukraine's failure to adequately address the issue. South Korea has demanded an official explanation, an apology and assurances against a recurrence af

results.title: Korean won inches down against US dollar ahead of Fed meeting
results.content: The Korean won edged down against the U.S. dollar Tuesday, as traders have kept a close watch on a Federal Reserve meeting this week. The won was quoted at 1,323.7 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., down 0.6 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. At one point in morning trading, the won advanced to a high of 1,322.8 won per dollar, helped by stronger-than-expected economic growth in the third quarter. The nation's economy grew 1 percent in the July-September period, thanks to semiconductor-led exports and investment. Foreign investors purchased a net 592.9 billion won ($447 million) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index gaining 3.09 percent to close at 5,638.34.

results.title: AMCHAM workshop explores AI-ready workforce, CEO risks
results.content: The American Chamber of Commerce in Korea (AMCHAM) held its HR Workshop 2026 at the Grand Hyatt Seoul on Tuesday, bringing together about 100 business leaders and professionals to discuss artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, workforce transformation and corporate risk management. Under the theme “AI-Ready Workforce: Leading People & Managing Risk in the Age of AI,” the workshop explored how companies can use AI to improve productivity and employee capabilities while addressing legal and organizational challenges. “AI is changing how we work. Our job as leaders is to make that change work for our businesses and our people,” AMCHAM Chairman and CEO James Kim said. “Employees need the skills and confidence to use [AI tools] well, while leaders need to set clear expectations and manage risk.” Rep. results.title: Hanmi Pharm Q3 net income down 69.1% to $10.6 mil.
results.content: Hanmi Pharm on Tuesday reported a third-quarter net income of 14 billion won ($10.6 million), down 69.1 percent from a year earlier. The Korean pharmaceutical company said in a regulatory filing that operating profit for the July-September period fell 31.3 percent on-year to 37.8 billion won. Revenue increased 4.2 percent to 377.4 billion won. The earnings failed to meet market expectations. The average estimate of net profit by analysts stood at 26.5 billion won, according to a survey by Yonhap Infomax, the financial data firm of Yonhap News Agency.

results.title: Ruling party decides to seek parliamentary probe into Supreme Court chief amid impeachment calls
results.content: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) said Tuesday it has decided to seek a parliamentary investigation into Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, with some hardliners calling for his impeachment over allegations of political interference. During a general meeting of its lawmakers, the DPK agreed to push for the probe, aiming to pass a related motion at a parliamentary plenary session scheduled for Thursday next week, DPK floor spokesperson Jeon Eun-su told reporters. The DPK has accused Cho of meddling in last year's presidential election after the Supreme Court overturned a not-guilty verdict in President Lee Jae Myung's election law violation case and sent it back to a lower court for retrial just ahead of the June 3 presidential election. The party also took issue with Cho's refusal to recommend a new candidate for Supreme Court justice as requested by the presidential office

results.title: Seoul stocks rebound as Anthropic IPO revives AI investment sentiment
results.content: Korean stocks rebounded Tuesday, led by gains in the country’s semiconductor heavyweights, as news of U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic’s planned blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) revived investor appetite after a recent pullback. The benchmark KOSPI opened at 5,658.65, up 3.46 percent from the previous close, according to the Korea Exchange. A buy-sidecar was triggered early in the session at 10:13 a.m., temporarily suspending program buy orders for five minutes after the market’s surge breached the volatility threshold. The index remained in positive territory throughout the session, closing at 5,638.34, up 3.09 percent. Foreign investors and institutions were net buyers of 835.9 billion won ($631.05 million) and 418.5 billion won, respectively, while retail investors sold a net 1. 4 trillion won. results.title: Chip boom fails to lift spending as private consumption falls
results.content: Korea's economy is growing on the back of a semiconductor export boom, but consumers aren't feeling the benefits. Private consumption fell 0.2 percent in the third quarter from the previous quarter, marking its first decline since the second quarter of 2023, according to preliminary data on third quarter economic growth from the Bank of Korea (BOK), Tuesday. Private spending growth had already slowed from 0.6 percent in the first quarter to 0.4 percent in the second before turning negative in the third. Spending declined for both goods, including cars and home appliances, and services, such as financial and dining services. The decline came even as the economy expanded 1 percent in the third quarter from the previous quarter, exceeding the central bank's forecast of 0.3 percent. results.title: [EXPLAINER] From Kim Young-sam to Lee Jae Myung: golf's enduring political trap
results.content: Golf has again become a political flashpoint in Korea after an opposition lawmaker’s allegation against first lady Kim Hea Kyung prompted an explicit denial from LPGA star Lydia Ko and a sharp rebuttal from Cheong Wa Dae. This episode drew fresh attention to why the sport remains so politically sensitive in Korea despite becoming more accessible to the public. Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) claimed that Kim received an exclusive golf lesson from Ko on Oct. 20 and released a video that featured a woman who Joo claimed is the golfer. Ko, a Korean-born New Zealand LPGA Hall of Fame member, denied any involvement, saying she attended an official sponsor event that day. results.title: Social media key to success for K-brands, AI expert says
results.content: Social media platforms have become a key marketplace for Korean beauty, food and fashion brands, and companies can leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to make their products go viral in global markets at minimal cost, according to an AI expert in Seoul Tuesday. Seldon Yoon, founder and CEO of Indent, a Seoul-based developer of commerce AI transformation (AX) solutions, said Reels and short-form content on Instagram and TikTok have become major channels for Korean consumers to discover and purchase new products. He added that creator content marketing has become more critical than ever, particularly for companies seeking to promote their products overseas and attract local consumers. Yoon, a former global e-commerce consultant for Samsung Electronics, cited a sharp increase in K-beauty exports since 2024 as evidence of successful overseas marketing. results.title: Kim's China trip may have been more than economic event: unification minister
results.content: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young said Tuesday that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un's trip to China last week may have been more than an economic event, given the makeup of his delegation. "The fact that both sides fielded their diplomatic and security teams deserves a close look," Chung said at a parliamentary audit, responding to a lawmaker's question about the meaning of Kim's surprise one-day trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday. He noted the North Korean delegation was heavy with diplomatic and security officials, and that no economic officials were present at the newly opened bridge over the Amnok River, known in China as the Yalu River. results.title: Marine Corps commander to visit Thailand for talks on defense cooperation
results.content: The commander of Korea's Marine Corps will visit Thailand this week to discuss expanding military and defense industry ties between the two countries, Korea's armed force said Tuesday. Lt. Gen. Ju Il-suk will make a four-day trip to Bangkok and Sattahip, an eastern coastal district home to Thailand's Marine Corps base, from Tuesday through Friday, the Marine Corps said in a media note. During the visit, Ju plans to hold bilateral talks with Rear Adm. Weerachai Leeka, commander of the Royal Thai Marine Corps, and other senior military officials to discuss efforts to strengthen military cooperation and expand defense industry partnership between the two armed forces. Ju will also pay tribute at a Korean War memorial in Chonburi, honoring Thai soldiers who fell while fighting alongside Korean forces during the 1950-53 conflict. results.title: Woman sentenced to 10-month prison term for spitting at police officer at election rally
results.content: A court on Tuesday sentenced a woman to 10 months in prison for spitting at a police officer and assaulting others during rallies to protest ballot shortages in June's local elections. The 45-year-old, surnamed Kim, was accused of assaulting a total of five people, including the police officer who was trying to restrain her, during rallies outside the Olympic Park Handball Gymnasium in southeastern Seoul on June 22 and 23. The Seoul Eastern District Court convicted her of obstruction of official duties and sentenced her to prison, citing her history of repeated assault and other offenses since February, as well as concerns she may reoffend. It also cited favorable factors in determining the level of punishment, including the fact that Kim admitted to her crimes, showed remorse and was diagnosed with bipolar disorder in 2024.

results.title: Korea should not sacrifice AI boom over chip dependence fears: IDB economist
results.content: Korea should capitalize on the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor boom rather than curb growth over concerns about its heavy reliance on chips, while building economic resilience through stabilization funds and greater structural flexibility, according to the chief economist of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), Tuesday. "I wouldn't kill the goose that lays the golden egg. It's weird to kill AI just because it's volatile. Let's find ways to adjust," Laura Alfaro, chief economist and economic counselor of the IDB, said during a press conference. "Right now, the game is AI, and Korea is growing faster than other countries. It happened because for many years you have built the production and infrastructure." results.title: LG Innotek Q3 net down 25.8% on fluctuating exchange rate
results.content: LG Innotek, an electronic components manufacturer under LG Group, said Tuesday its third-quarter net profit fell 25.8 percent from a year earlier, as exchange-rate fluctuations weighed on profitability. Net profit for the July-September period came to 95.2 billion won ($71.9 million), down 128.4 billion won from a year earlier, the company said in a regulatory filing. LG Innotek said its net profit declined as the Korean won weakened against the U.S. dollar when it purchased raw materials in the first half of the year but strengthened sharply by the time the company began mass-producing and shipping products in the third quarter. Operating profit for the cited period fell 53.4 percent on-year to 94.8 billion won. results.title: Seoul mayor's acquittal offers chance for PPP housecleaning
results.content: Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon saw the clouds that loomed over his political career all but disappear Friday. An appellate court acquitted the five-term mayor of violating the Political Funds Act over allegations that a supporter paid for his opinion polling. Had the ruling not been overturned and he had been slapped with a fine of 1 million won ($755) or more, Oh would have been unseated and barred from running for elected office for five years. The mayor wore a broad smile, just like when he was reelected in the June 3 local elections. His fifth-term win was unexpected, bumping up the prospects of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP). A Supreme Court ruling is pending, but the appellate court's reversal in itself speaks of a brighter political future for Oh and the PPP on the path to the 2030 presidential election. results.title: Special panel seeks to question ex-President Yoon over 2022 crowd crush
results.content: A special commission investigating the deadly 2022 Itaewon crowd crush plans to question former President Yoon Suk Yeol over the government's handling of the disaster, officials said Tuesday. The National Commission for the Investigation of the October 29 Itaewon Disaster outlined its plan to question the jailed ex-president and former Interior Minister Lee Sang-min in December as it shared the interim results of its probe. The commission is tasked with uncovering the cause of the tragedy, which happened during Halloween festivities in Seoul's nightlife district of Itaewon on Oct. 29, 2022, when crowds surged into a narrow alley, leaving 159 people dead and 196 injured. The panel found various shortcomings in the government response to the disaster. results.title: Samsung Electronics chief to visit robotics R&D center on 4th anniversary of inauguration
results.content: Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong is set to visit the company's robotics business hub Tuesday, industry sources said, as the tech giant steps up efforts to develop robotics as a key growth engine for the future. Lee is scheduled to visit the company's research and development (R&D) center in central Seoul, in a move seen as underscoring his commitment to new businesses through on-site management, they said. Tuesday marks the fourth anniversary of Lee's inauguration as chairman in 2022. His visit to a key robotics facility, a business he has identified as a major future growth driver for Samsung, is seen as signaling the company's commitment to expand into new sectors. Lee is expected to review preparations for robotics technologies to be unveiled at CES 2027, the world's largest consumer electronics and IT trade show, in Las Vegas in January. results.title: PPP urges Cheong Wa Dae to clarify first lady's golf allegations
results.content: The main opposition People Power Party (PPP) on Tuesday urged the presidential office to clarify allegations that first lady Kim Hea Kyung received private golf lessons from a prominent professional golfer at a military-run golf course. PPP floor leader Jeong Jeom-sig said Cheong Wa Dae should establish the facts surrounding allegations over the first lady's golf lessons, which were first disclosed by PPP lawmaker Joo Jin-woo earlier this week. Joo alleged Monday that the wife of President Lee Jae Myung received "imperial-style" golf lessons from a world-renowned golfer at Taereung Golf Club in northern Seoul on Oct. 20, the day when a man in his 70s set fire to two buildings in southern Seoul, leaving five people seriously injured and 14 others with minor injuries.
